prompt_text: My roof has hail damage in Denver. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t browse the web right now to pull up current company listings, so I can’t give you a live list of specific Denver roofers. I can, however, give you a quick, practical plan so you’ll know exactly which types of companies to call, how to find the best local options, and what to ask so you pick a reputable contractor for hail damage.

Who to call (call 3–5):
- A local manufacturer‑certified roofer (e.g., a GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred or CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster) — why: manufacturer certification means trained installers and enhanced manufacturer warranties. Search those directories for “Denver” or your ZIP.
- A local independent roofer with strong local reviews and an established business address (4+ stars on Google, positive BBB rating, long local history) — why: local contractors are familiar with Denver codes, storm permitting, and common hail issues.
- A restoration/insurance‑claims specialist who works frequently with insurance companies — why: they know how to document damage for claims and handle adjusters; useful if you plan to file a claim.
- Optionally, one national company with a local branch (if present) for comparison — why: they can have broad resources and standardized processes, but compare cost and local reputation.

How to find specific names quickly (search tips):
- Search manufacturer directories: “GAF Master Elite contractors near [ZIP]”, “Owens Corning Preferred contractor Denver”, “CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster Denver.”
- Check Google Maps, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor and BBB for “roofing hail damage Denver” and sort by rating + recent reviews.
- Ask neighbors, HOA, or local Facebook/Nextdoor for referrals after the same hailstorm.
- Call your insurance company and ask for names of local contractors they’ve worked with (but don’t feel obligated to use them).

Red flags / what to avoid:
- Door‑to‑door “storm chasers” who pressure you to sign immediately.
- No local office or only a P.O. box.
- Contractor won’t show proof of CO general liability insurance and workers’ comp.
- Extremely low bid that’s far below others.
- Requests for large upfront payment (more than 25–30%) or cash‑only deals.

What to ask every contractor (ask for these in writing):
- Are you licensed to work in Colorado? What is your license/registration number?
- Proof of general liability insurance and workers’ comp — ask for certificates.
- Are you manufacturer‑certified? Which brands and what warranties do you offer?
- Do you have experience with insurance claims and will you meet my adjuster?
- Will you pull local permits and handle inspections?
- Detailed written estimate: scope of work, materials (brand/type), underlayment, ventilation, flashing, disposal, timeline, cleanup.
- Warranty: workmanship warranty length and what it covers.
- Request 3 recent local references and photos of completed hail‑damage jobs.

How to compare estimates:
- Confirm all bids use the same scope and comparable materials.
- Compare total price, warranty, and the contractor’s response time.
- Ask who will be on site (subs?) and confirm lien waiver on final payment.
- Check reviews and BBB complaints history.

Immediate steps if you suspect hail damage:
- Take clear dated photos of roof, gutters, siding, and vehicles.
- Contact your insurer to report the claim (if you plan to claim).
- Get at least three written estimates before signing anything.
- Consider a temporary tarp only if there is active leakage—only by a licensed contractor.

If you want, do one of these and I’ll help next:
- Tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll give you exact search phrases and directories to run (so you can pull current, local names).
- Paste 3–5 company names you find and I’ll evaluate them against the checklist and point out questions to ask each one.

Which would you prefer?
